motivation: The 43 by 43 development tournament is exactly seat-complementary. The season-one rule beat season-twelve search on 65.625% of available points, the search beat the first-trade table on 62.5%, and that table beat the rule on 67.1875%. Optimizing a mixture on four old development donors improved worst-opponent score on the other four from 0.4375 to 0.475. Reversing the donor halves improved it from 0.375 to 0.4375. Average score declined in both. Test whether a player who changes styles between complete rounds is harder to counter.
test: Before the joint native selection begins, freeze the average of the two development solutions and an independent preassigned component for every opponent, seat, RTT and repeat, using separate RNG seeds 118001 for native and 118019 for simulator. A scheduled mixture observation uses the actual result of that assigned frozen component. Also report the expected mixture score from all component cells, with no post-outcome switching. No extra native bouts or duplicate observations are counted. The 40 native selected rounds and 160 simulated selected rounds use the original W-tap, Hold-W and singleton comparison field. This supplementary sub-study cannot replace the registered native selection winner.
